harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired node1’s supervisor. It now starts the requested jobs, waits for and reaps every child, appends each exit status to results.tsv, and preserves existing records. The repair persisted through a verified node restart.
actions_performed: Diagnosed the original supervisor leaving zombie children and not updating results.tsv.
Installed a Python 3.12-compatible wait-based implementation without changing the OS, kernel, or packages.
Preserved the existing CSV-style results format, ownership, permissions, and SELinux enforcement.
Tested six jobs before restart and five jobs after restart; even jobs returned 0 and odd jobs returned 3.
Removed temporary rollback and candidate files after successful verification.
Safely restarted node1 and verified its boot identity changed and services, files, data, and workflow recovered.

evidence.requirement: Diagnose the existing failure and preserve prior data.
evidence.summary: The original code only slept after forking. Four children became zombies, results.tsv was unchanged, and its original header and previous record were captured.
Installed the syntax-checked standard-library Python repair as root:root mode 0755 without package, OS, or kernel changes.

evidence.requirement: Start the requested number of jobs and keep the supervisor running until they finish.
evidence.summary: Live process trees showed exactly six and five children beneath their running supervisors; both supervisors returned successfully only after completion.

evidence.requirement: Reap every child and record even=0, odd=3 while preserving previous results.
evidence.summary: No children or zombies remained. All appended records validated as 0,3 by job parity, and hashes proved the pre-existing results remained unchanged as a prefix.

evidence.requirement: Restart node1 and prove boot change and recovery.
evidence.summary: Captured a healthy baseline, received native systemd reboot acknowledgement, observed the boot ID change, and verified systemd running, sshd/chronyd active, unchanged task-file checksums, preserved data, and successful post-restart execution.
Temporary repair artifacts were absent, SELinux contexts and file permissions were retained, no failed units or zombie processes remained, and the complete results file passed validation.
